newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk villagers protest against gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Turk villagers protest against gold mine.

text.p: Turkish villagers protested on Friday against a mining company felling olive trees to open space for a new gold mine near the coastal town of Bergama in western Turkey, witnesses said.

A crowd of 3,000-5,000 blocked a road connecting Izmir and Canakkale provinces in protest at the mining plans of Eurogold Madencilik A.S., a subsidiary of the Australian-French venture Mine Or SA and Inmet Mining Corporation of Canada.
The gold mine in Ovacik village, 12 km (seven miles) from Bergama, is expected to produce 110,000 ounces of gold annually.
The mine has been opposed strongly on environmental grounds because of concerns about the impact on people's health and the local flora of cyanide used in the extraction of gold.
They say the possible leakage of cyanide into drinking water and soil could destroy the terrain or have carcinogenic effects.
In March, the Turkish Environment Ministry approved the mining plans of Eurogold, which made an initial application six years ago.
